findings.title: Dynamic imports are started eagerly for every app
findings.body: Every value in the appStore object literal is an import() call, so all 28 calls are evaluated as soon as this module is loaded. Code that needs only one app (for example getCalendar for a single credential) therefore still starts loading every calendar, video, CRM, and payment app and retains all of their side effects and memory/startup cost, defeating the intended per-app lazy loading. A rejected import for an app that is never used can also surface later as an unhandled rejection from the cached promise. Store thunks such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` and invoke the thunk at lookup time instead.

findings.title: Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletion fire-and-forget
findings.body: The forEach callback was made async to await getCalendar, but Array.prototype.forEach ignores the returned promises. Reschedule therefore proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true without waiting for calendar.deleteEvent or deleteMeeting to even start (the await on getCalendar defers them past the forEach), so in a request-scoped/serverless execution the old events can be left behind, and any rejection becomes an unhandled rejection that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a for...of loop.

findings.body: The forEach callback was made async to await getCalendar, but Array.prototype.forEach ignores the returned promises. Reschedule therefore proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true without waiting for calendar.deleteEvent or deleteMeeting to even start (the await on getCalendar defers them past the forEach), so in a request-scoped/serverless execution the old events can be left behind, and any rejection becomes an unhandled rejection that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a for...of loop.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not wait for old calendar/video deletion
findings.body: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach now takes an async callback whose promise is discarded. Immediately afterwards the mutation sends the reschedule email and webhooks and returns, while the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent and deleteMeeting work is still pending; it may be abandoned when the request ends and its failures are unhandled, leaving the supposedly cancelled calendar event and video meeting active. Await the deletions with Promise.all over map (or a for...of loop) before continuing.

findings.title: Recurring-cancellation deletions can miss the later Promise.all entirely
findings.body: For recurring bookings, calendar deletions are collected by pushing into apiDeletes from inside an async forEach callback that first awaits getCalendar and then awaits deleteEvent before pushing. The handler later awaits Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)), but concat snapshots apiDeletes at that moment, typically before those async callbacks have pushed anything. The handler can therefore delete the booking's attendees/references (losing the external uids needed to retry) and return while the external calendar deletions are not awaited or have not run, orphaning events on users' calendars. Collect the deletion promises synchronously via map/Promise.all or a sequential for...of and await them before the database cleanup completes.
